reviews.head: 2d7ac626
reviews.note: I found two blocking defects: the scheduled pull silently drops logs if the backlog exceeds the 1,000-log page limit, and the analytics query silently underreports the 7-day totals if there are more than 10,000 calls.

findings.text: If a pull hits `MAX_PAGES` before reaching the last mark (e.g. after a spike of >1,000 calls), `fetchNewLogs` returns the newest 1,000 logs and `pullGateway` unconditionally advances the mark to the newest of them, permanently dropping all older unread logs.

`windowSql` selects individual rows with a hard limit of 10,000; if there are more than 10,000 calls in the 7-day window, older calls are silently omitted from the query result, causing the Models page and CLI to underreport the window's true total cost, tokens, and calls.

If the `METRICS` binding is somehow missing or misconfigured, `writeLog` returns false and writes nothing, but the mark is still advanced, meaning those logs will be skipped forever once the binding is fixed.

reviews.head: 04cafbf6
reviews.note: The earlier blocking findings are resolved (a capped pull records its gap, totals are summed in SQL without a row limit, and writing oldest-first prevents advancing the mark on failure), but a new data-loss defect was found where pagination stops prematurely and drops older logs if the API returns invalid logs on a full page.

findings.text: `fetchNewLogs` uses the filtered `found.length < PAGE_SIZE` to stop paging; if the API returns a full page of 50 logs but one fails to parse (e.g., missing ID), `found.length` is less than 50, causing the pull to stop prematurely, return `gap: null`, and silently drop all older valid logs without recording a gap.

reviews.head: d7fa6484
reviews.note: I read the whole diff and the sandbox runner: the new render host lets any project's check container have Browser Run load any HTML, with JavaScript on, no request filter, and label text returned in the reply, which is a two-way way out of a sandbox meant to have no Internet; the follow-ups are about tests that skip instead of failing, thin rule coverage and stale comments.

findings.text: The gateway gives sandbox-supplied HTML to Browser Run with JavaScript on and no allowRequestPattern or rejectRequestPattern, and sends label text back in `problems`, so code in any project's check container can fetch any Internet URL through the browser and read the response, with no limit on use. This widens the sandbox's npm-GET-only egress. The comment at wrangler.jsonc:36 says the sessions only allow the pages' font hosts, but the code sets no such limit.
Any non-200 answer from /check, including 502 when the scrape fails or the binding is missing, turns into a skip instead of a failure, so a render check that breaks still shows as passing.
Outside the sandbox the check always skips, so the checks that passed on the agent's machine never actually rendered anything; the layout rules are covered by one overflow case in the spec only.
The header says test/render-check.test.ts covers the geometry rules, but that file doesn't exist and no test covers the overlap, outside-the-drawing, narrow-width or public-bar rules.
`per` is computed from width alone and used for y and height too, which is only right when the SVG keeps its aspect ratio (preserveAspectRatio not set to none).

reviews.head: 876eea58
reviews.note: I verified that all earlier blocking findings are resolved: the browser sandbox enforces request restrictions, non-200 responses now correctly fail the test, geometry logic is robust and rigorously covered by the new spec file, and SVG dimensions appropriately handle aspect ratios.

findings.text: If the browser normalizes multiple spaces within a `class` attribute into a single space, `sent.includes(cls)` could fail and fall back to naming it "an element" despite the class being sent.

t313.title: Kimi's t275 runs died on 'Provider returned error' (2026-10-08): the AI Gateway logs show 12 HTTP 400s, each 'maximum context length is 262144 tokens... 230145 input tokens' plus 32000 output, because ~/.config/opencode/openrouter-api.json and deepseek-api.json gave the paid models no limit.context, so opencode never compacted (fixed by hand in the config the same day). (1) atelier runner warns at start, as t289 does for jobs, when a configured opencode model has no limit.context and its provider is a custom one models.dev cannot fill; (2) when a build or review run ends on a provider error, the runner reads the error body (from opencode's output or the gateway log by cf-aig-metadata) and records its reason in the run report (context overflow, auth, rate limit, provider down), so a model's failures say whether they were ours or theirs
